name: Red Pink
lede: Red Pink is a hot, coral-leaning pink, built from [[red]] plus [[pink]] in the 2010 xkcd color survey.

sections.title: A plain compound, an older printed phrase
sections.body:
The survey pairs red directly with pink, its simplest modifier grammar [1]. As a color name on file, 2010 is the earliest record; the ISCC-NBS system would place it among the deep yellowish pinks, though at a loose fit, 9.4 units off [1]. In printed English, though, the phrase "red pink" itself goes back further: our Ngram data finds it from 1800, peaking in use around 1930, long before the survey used it as a single color name [3].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[pink-red]], its own word order reversed, just 2.8 units away and almost the same shade [2]. [[neon-red]] and [[pinkish-red]] sit close behind, both nearly identical as well [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive matches this color across even a small share of its canvas, as photographed [3]. Its high chroma makes it an unlikely survivor on an aged, varnished canvas [3]. The phrase's printed peak in the 1930s, by contrast, has nothing to do with paint; it tracks English usage of the words, not any dye or pigment [3].

origin.first_recorded: 2010 xkcd color survey; the phrase "red pink" in print from 1800
